facts.statement: The species Remiornis heberti was first described by Lemoine in 1881.
The genus Remiornis was originally established by Martin in 1992.
Remiornis heberti is an extinct bird from the Paleocene period found in France.
facts.quote: Remiornis heberti is an extinct species of paleognath bird from the Paleocene of France.

facts.statement: Remiornis heberti was comparable in size to modern rheas.
facts.quote: It is a species comparable in size to modern rheas

facts.statement: Remiornis heberti is possibly related to the European Paleogene ratite Palaeotis.
facts.quote: possibly related to another European Paleogene ratite, Palaeotis

facts.statement: Remiornis belongs to the family Remiornithidae.
Remiornis lived during the Thanetian stage, between 59.24 and 56 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Thanetian to Thanetian (59.24 to 56 million years ago)
